_readme: Golden canonical signing payloads for COMPOSITION certification records (CompositionCertificationRecordSigner). These bytes are the message every composition admission signature is computed over, so they are pinned here and read by the in-repo golden test. To regenerate a case deliberately, copy the actual payload the failing test prints into this file. Regenerate ONLY when the canonical form is deliberately changed, and understand that changing it invalidates every composition signature already written. Doubles are emitted in ONE canonical form - 17 significant digits on the invariant culture, both zeros collapsed onto 0, NaN and the infinities refused outright - the same form and the same decisions as the brick lane, because the decimal form a target's own formatter produces is not the same on all of them. See CertificationRecordSigning.WriteNumberOrNull; the awkward-double cases below pin it here.

cases.name: composition-populated
cases.why: Every field carrying a non-default value, plus the two the composition payload must structurally exclude (signature, gate). Structural mutant id lists are supplied out of order to pin that the lists are sorted at all - these ids collate the same way under ordinal and culture rules, so which comparer does the sorting is pinned by the composition-mutant-id-ordering case below rather than by this one. The reason string pins the escaping of quote, angle brackets, ampersand, apostrophe, plus and non-ASCII.

record.reason: golden fixture — quote " angle < & > apostrophe ' plus + café

cases.payload: {"status":"PASS","stage":"S0-S2","admitted":true,"signed":true,"timestamp":"2026-01-02T03:04:05.1234567Z","compositionId":"golden-composition","compositionEscapeRate":0.5,"totalStructuralMutants":7,"survivingStructuralMutants":2,"killedStructuralMutantIds":["m-1","m-10","m-2"],"survivingStructuralMutantIds":["s-1","s-2"],"reason":"golden fixture \u2014 quote \u0022 angle \u003C \u0026 \u003E apostrophe \u0027 plus \u002B caf\u00E9"}

cases.name: composition-mutant-id-ordering
cases.why: Structural mutant ids chosen so that ordinal and culture collation disagree: ordinal compares UTF-16 code units, so every uppercase initial sorts ahead of every lowercase one, where culture rules order the same ids alphabetically and case-blind. Ordinal gives B-1 before a-2 and S-2 before s-1; culture rules give the reverse of both. Ids that read like real mutant ids sort identically under either comparer, which is why they pin that a sort happens but not which comparer performs it.

cases.name: composition-minimal
cases.why: Only the required members. Pins that the payload still carries all 12 names with null values and empty arrays - a small payload is legitimate, an empty one is not.

cases.name: composition-escaping
cases.why: Non-ASCII, a control character, a surrogate pair, a tab, and every character the default JavaScript encoder escapes - in compositionId and reason. Pins the encoder and its uppercase hex.

cases.name: composition-awkward-double
cases.why: The composition lane carries the same kind of double and the same emitter decision, so it is pinned the same way: 1/3 as compositionEscapeRate, the value whose decimal form differed between targets before one canonical form was chosen.

cases.name: composition-zero-signs
cases.why: Negative zero on the composition lane. -0 emits 0, for the reason spelled out on the brick lane's v2-zero-signs case: a signed zero makes the writers agree and leaves the readers disagreeing.
